[b]Ziel[/b]\nFühre deine kleine Siedlung:
[b]Goal[/b]
Guide your little settlement through the generations. Provide food, build huts and let your island grow.

[b]Controls[/b]
Drag to move the map; use the mouse wheel or two fingers to zoom and pan. On a PC you can also use WASD or the arrow keys. Tap settlers, buildings or resources for info.

[b]Goals[/b]
Your next goal is always shown at the top left. Tap it for an explanation. Every goal you reach brings a reward, and new ones keep coming.

[b]Sound[/b]
Set the music and sound volume in the menu.

[b]Settlers[/b]
Every settler has their own skills. In the info window, give them a job that fits their strengths. With practice they get better. Idle settlers help wherever they are needed.

[b]Character[/b]
Every settler is different: clever or simple, sturdy or sickly, hard-working or easygoing, cheerful or grumpy. Each one also has talents (marked with + in the info window): they learn faster in those. Clever settlers learn and research faster. Children inherit part of their character from their parents and learn a lot at school, especially in their talents.

[b]Health[/b]
Settlers get sick: a cold slows them down, with fever or dysentery they stay in bed and can die. The sickly, the old, children, the hungry, the freezing and anyone sleeping outside fall ill more easily, and the sick infect others. Vitamins from berries, apples and coconuts protect them; anyone who goes without for a long time gets scurvy. Medicine helps the sick recover faster.

[b]Mood and work power[/b]
Being full and healthy, varied food and a nice home lift the mood; hunger, sickness, cold and grief lower it. Cheerful settlers work faster and have children more often. Work power in the info window shows how fast a settler is working right now.

[b]Leisure[/b]
At first, settlers know nothing but work. The more developed your settlement is (see Lifestyle in the settler list), the more leisure they want: chatting by the fire, walking on the beach, playing with children or reading. If they get none, they are overworked and in a bad mood. During a famine, everyone works without a break.

[b]Food[/b]
Settlers eat at the campfire. Each food fills them up differently and brings a different amount of vitamins: berries, apples and coconuts barely fill them up but are full of vitamins. Bread, smoked fish and meat keep them full for a long time but have hardly any vitamins. Raw grain is not very filling; a mill and bakery turn it into good bread.
Hungry settlers work slower and eventually starve. Settlers who get too few vitamins also work slower, get sick more easily and get scurvy. So provide filling food and fruit. A settler's window shows their vitamins. If the storehouse is empty, hungry settlers eat straight from the bush or at the shore. Gathering spots are quickly picked clean and only regrow slowly.

[b]Children[/b]
Children are only born when there is free housing in huts and enough food in storage. In wooden houses, children are born 40 % more often, in stone houses 80 %. Children grow up after 3 days, twice as fast with a school (Teaching research). Nobody lives forever, so make sure to have children in time.

[b]Building[/b]
Choose a building and a building site. Builders and idle settlers bring the materials and build it. Huts and wooden houses can be upgraded later in the info window.

[b]Research[/b]
In the tech tree you choose what your settlers learn next. Researchers think at the campfire, and much faster in the writing room and library. Every research unlocks new buildings or makes work easier. Eight ages with sixteen tiers lead through the history of humankind: Stone Age, Antiquity, Middle Ages, Renaissance, Industrial Age, Modern Age, Information Age and Future. The university, research lab and AI center research faster and faster. You only see later ages once the previous one is reached.

[b]New ages[/b]
Glass, paper, steel, machines, power and electronics are made in new workshops. Power plants, solar parks and fusion reactors supply the power that the electronics plant and AI center need. Apartment houses and apartment blocks offer lots of housing, and greenhouses yield crops even in winter. Once an AI center stands, the artificial intelligence assigns idle settlers to the jobs that are currently missing. The future city is the goal of all ages.

[b]Workshops[/b]
The saw pit, mill, bakery, brickworks and others turn raw materials into better goods. Cooks work in the mill, bakery, smokehouse and chicken farm, craftsmen in the workshops, stonecutters in the quarry, clay pit and mine. Tap the supplies at the top to see all goods.

[b]Storage[/b]
Every storehouse has storage space: the campfire 200, a storehouse 400, a large store 1000. Big goods need more space than small ones: a plank 3, wood and stone 2, berries 1. Tap the supplies at the top or "Storage settings" in the storehouse and use − and + to set how much of each good is stored. That amount is then reserved for the good. Goods set to "free" share the remaining space. If there is no more room for a good, settlers stop gathering it. If you have too much of a good, you can throw away the surplus; it is then lost.

[b]Variety[/b]
If there are at least three kinds of food in storage, children are born more often.

[b]Seafaring[/b]
Every island has its own storage. Goods only reach another island by ship. With the Shipbuilding research you build a shipyard on the shore; in the shipyard window you choose the next ship. Rowboats are small and land on any beach, cogs carry a lot, clippers are fast, galleons are huge. Every ship needs sailors (the Sailor job) and a berth in its home port: shipyard 1, jetty 2, harbor 2, large harbor 3, quays 1. Cogs and clippers only call at islands with a harbor, galleons only at large harbors. Wood, ore and food quays load their goods three times as fast.

[b]Sea chart and routes[/b]
The Islands button opens the sea chart. "Send ship here" brings settlers and goods to an island, "Find new island" sends a ship exploring. Under "Ships" you set routes: at each stop the ship loads the selected goods and unloads everything else, then sails on, again and again.

[b]New islands[/b]
Palm islands have coconuts and lots of fish, forest islands mushrooms and wood, rock islands ore and gold. You need gold for the highest research. The farther out, the more wild animals.

[b]Wild animals[/b]
Wolves, wild boars and bears live in dens and caves. Settlers flee from them into houses, and wolves are especially dangerous at night. With Weapons, settlers become hunters and you can build watchtowers. Hunters bring meat and furs and clear out the dens so no more animals come.

[b]Watch out[/b]
If the last settler on an island dies, that island is lost forever. The game is only over once all islands are lost. The world is endless: there is always another island to discover.
